texts.preamble: Mr. Ram Krishna Mudholkar, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 21 February, 2022 Author: Chillakur Sumalatha Bench: Chillakur Sumalatha In The High Court For The State Of Telangana At Hyderabad ***** Criminal Petition No.2936 Of 2013 Between: Mr. Ram Krishna Mudholkar ...Petitioner/Accused No.3 And 1. The State of Andhra Pradesh, rep. by its Public Prosecutor, Hyderabad. 2. Smt. S. Shilpa, Agricultural Officer, O/o. Ada, Hyderabad, Ranga Reddy District.
texts.facts: 2. Seeking to quash the proceedings that are initiated against the petitioner, who is arrayed as accused No.3 in C.C.No.784 of 2012 that is pending on the file of the Court of I Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Nampally, Hyderabad, the petitioner filed the present application. 5. The case of the complainant, as could be seen from the complaint, is that on 14.03.2011, the Agricultural Officer (Technical), Hyderabad, visited the premises of M/s. Vanasri Seeds Pvt. Ltd., which is located in D.No.3-6- 308/1, Hyderguda, Hyderabad and has drawn six insecticide samples. The samples drawn were duly sealed 5 Dr.CSL,J CRL.P.NO.2936 OF 2013 and packed, as provided under law and a report was also prepared. The said samples were sent to Insecticide Analyst for analysis. The Insecticide Analyst declared Fenazaquin 10% EC as misbranded. By the time the Analyst report was received, the sample got expired. Therefore, there was no chance for reanalysis of the sample. Thus, the accused including the petitioner, who is arrayed as accused No.3, have committed the offences punishable under Section 29(1)(a) of the Insecticides Act, 1968.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the complaint itself is not maintainable as per the contents of the Insecticides Act, 1968 and therefore, continuation of proceedings against the petitioner, who is accused No.3 in 4 Dr.CSL,J CRL.P.NO.2936 OF 2013 the said Calendar Case, is unwarranted and therefore, the same has to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. Mr. Ram Krishna Mudholkar, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 21 February, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107593384/ 2 3. On the other hand, learned Public Prosecutor submits that on analysis, the sample drawn was found to be misbranded and therefore, a complaint was lodged by the Agricultural Officer, Hyderabad, against the petitioner and others and therefore, the present petition is unsustainable. It is also laid down that the Insecticide Inspector has to deliver one copy of the report to the person from whom the sample was taken. It is further narrated that the said person, within a period of 28 days from the date of receipt of copy of the report, can exhibit his intention to adduce evidence in contravention of the report. Section 24(4) of the Insecticides Act, 1968, further states that when such person exhibits his intention to adduce evidence in contravention of the Insecticide Analyst report, the Court may on its own motion or in its discretion at the request either of the complainant or of the accused, cause the sample of the insecticide sent for test or analysis to the Central Insecticide Laboratory. For the convenience of discussion and fruitful analysis, Section 24 of the Insecticides Act, 1968 is extracted as under: Report of Insecticide Analyst:- (1) The Insecticide Analyst to whom a sample of any insecticide has been submitted for test or analysis under sub-section (6) of Section 22, shall, within a period of thirty days, deliver to the Insecticide Inspector Mr. Ram Krishna Mudholkar, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 21 February, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107593384/ 3 7 Dr.CSL,J CRL.P.NO.2936 OF 2013 submitting it a signed report in duplicate in the prescribed form. (2) The Insecticide Inspector on receipt thereof shall deliver one copy of the report to the person form whom the sample was taken and shall retain the other copy for use in any prosecution in respect of the sample. (3) Any document purporting to be a report signed by an Insecticide Analyst shall be evidence of the facts stated therein, and such evidence shall be conclusive unless the person from whom the sample was taken has within twenty-eight days of the receipt of a copy of the report notified in writing the Insecticide Inspector or the court before which any proceedings in respect of the sample are pending that he intends to adduce evidence in controversion of the report. (4) Unless the sample has already been tested or analyzed in the Central Laboratory, where a person has under sub-section (3) notified his intention of adducing evidence in controversion of the Insecticide Analyst's report, the Court may, of its own motion or in its discretion at the request either of the complainant or of the accused, cause the sample of the insecticide produced before the Magistrate under sub-section (6) of section 22 to be sent for test or analysis to the said laboratory, (which shall, within a period of thirty days, which shall make the test or analysis) and report in writing signed by, or under the authority of, the Director of the Central Insecticides Laboratory the result thereof, and such report shall be conclusive evidence of the facts stated therein." 8 Dr.CSL,J CRL.P.NO.2936 OF 2013 (5) The cost of a test or analysis made by the Central Insecticides Laboratory under sub- section (4) shall be paid by the complainant or the accused, as the court shall direct." 7. 9. Catena of decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court and this Court emphasizes that there is every requirement that the samples drawn be tested either by the State Analyst notified for that purpose or by the Central Analyst within its shelf life. Submitting that in similar situations, Mr. Ram Krishna Mudholkar, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 21 February, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107593384/ 4 the Hon'ble Apex Court held that the proceedings are unsustainable as the valuable right of the accused for getting the sample reanalyzed is lost due to the acts of the complainant, learned counsel for the petitioner relied upon three decisions. The first decision is the one that is rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Gupta Chemicals Private Limited and Others v. State of 10 Dr.CSL,J CRL.P.NO.2936 OF 2013 Rajasthan and another1 wherein the Court at paragraph Nos.11 to 13 of the judgment held as follows:- "From our perusal of the afore quoted provisions it is manifest that ordinarily in the absence of any material to the contrary, the report of the insecticides analyst will be accepted as final and conclusive of the material contained therewith. The High Court was not right in 1 (2010) 7 SCC 735 11 Dr.CSL,J CRL.P.NO.2936 OF 2013 dismissing the petition filed under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. Accordingly , the appeals are allowed, the orders passed by the High Court are [LEAKAGE_MASK] and the prosecution alleged against the appellants are [LEAKAGE_MASK]." The second one is the decision rendered by the same Court in the case between Northern Mineral Limited v. Union of india and another2, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court at paragraph No.25 held as follows: "It may be mentioned herein that shelf life of the insecticides had expired even prior to the filing of the complaint. The position therefore which emerges is that by sheer inaction the shelf life of the sample of insecticides had expired and for that reason no step was possible to be taken for its test and analysis by Central Insecticides Mr. Ram Krishna Mudholkar, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 21 February, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107593384/ 5 Laboratory. The third decision is also from the Hon'ble Apex Court in a case between State of Haryana v. Unique Farmaid Ltd. and Others3, wherein the Court at paragraph No.12 held as follows: "It cannot be gainsaid, therefore, that the respondents in these appeals have been deprived of their valuable right to have the sample tested from the Central Insecticides Laboratory under Sub- 2 (2010) 7 SCC 726 3 (1999) 8 SCC 190 12 Dr.CSL,J CRL.P.NO.2936 OF 2013 section (4) of Section 24 of the Act.
